originalSummary: Once environment variables are checked, you must complete steps specific to systems that have Onboard Key Manager \(OKM\), NetApp Storage Encryption \(NSE\) or NetApp Volume Encryption \(NVE\) enabled.
fixedSummary: Once environment variables are checked, you must complete steps specific to systems that have Onboard Key Manager OKM, NetApp Storage Encryption NSE or NetApp Volume Encryption NVE enabled.

originalSummary: The boot media stores a primary and secondary set of system \(boot image\) files that the system uses when it boots. Depending on your network configuration, you can perform either a nondisruptive or disruptive replacement.
fixedSummary: The boot media stores a primary and secondary set of system boot image files that the system uses when it boots. Depending on your network configuration, you can perform either a nondisruptive or disruptive replacement.

originalSummary: All other components in the system must be functioning properly; if not, you must contact technical support.
fixedSummary: To replace the chassis, you must remove the components from the impaired chassis and install them in the replacement chassis.

originalSummary: All other components in the system must be functioning properly; if not, you must contact technical support.
fixedSummary: To replace the chassis, you must remove the power supplies, fans, controller modules, I/O modules, DCPM modules, and USB LED module from the impaired chassis and install them in the replacement chassis.

originalSummary: To hot-swap a destage controller power module \(DCPM\), which contains the NVRAM11 battery, you must locate the failed DCPM module, remove it from the chassis, and install the replacement DCPM module.
fixedSummary: To hot-swap a destage controller power module DCPM, which contains the NVRAM11 battery, you must locate the failed DCPM module, remove it from the chassis, and install the replacement DCPM module.

originalSummary: You must replace a DIMM in the controller module when your system registers an increasing number of correctable error correction codes (ECC); failure to do so causes a system panic.
fixedSummary: You must replace a DIMM in the controller when your storage system encounters errors such as excessive CECC errors that are based on Health Monitor alerts or uncorrectable ECC errors, typically caused by a single DIMM failure preventing the storage system from booting ONTAP.
